title: ROOTSIGNAL
tagline: Heal the land. Break the machines.
pitch: A solarpunk action RPG. Wear living technology that grows stronger as the land heals, move through a fight like a wave, and tear the machines of occupation apart.
status: In development by Greenfire. Early build, first playtests now.

story.title: Five generations after the Hard Seasons
paragraphs: The Alder Watershed came back. Where there were dust and ration lines there are now eco villages: living architecture, repair workshops, seed libraries, shared kitchens and music at the long tables after sunset.

Then the Bastion Directorate arrived. Born from emergency logistics, it never stood down. Now it leases and seizes farmland to build the Continuity Corridor, a chain of army data centers that run drones, surveillance and predictive control.

On an old farm at the edge of Alder Fields, Elias Vale's machines keep failing in the same strip of ground, and lights hang in the air over the broken soil. The land remembers, and it has interests of its own.

You are Rook. You grew up here, trained as a field systems specialist, and came home after an assignment went wrong. You are about to become the bridge between a farmer, a resistance, a community and something far older than all of them.

items.title: A transmission
items.text: The resistance's call across the watershed, passed hand to hand when the networks are watched.

items.title: An anomaly
items.text: Readings no instrument should take, rising from the same strip of farmland where the machines keep dying.

items.title: A way of listening
items.text: Elias's own word for what happens when he stops talking and lets the land answer.

items.title: A question
items.text: Asked of you, the player. What do you owe a place that remembers you?

spirits.title: The Chorus
spirits.text: The spirits are real, and there are many of them. Outsiders call them the Chorus. They appear as drifting orbs, they speak in fragments through Elias, and they talk about places and relationships, never tactics. They are not a power source, and they are not yours to use. The Bastion Directorate has noticed them, and it wants them to behave.

world.title: The Alder Watershed
world.intro: Compact and connected. Every district has a safe settlement, a contested site, and a way you leave it better than you found it.

districts.name: Alder Fields
districts.text: Farms, orchards, terraces and Elias's homestead, around the village of Greenhaven Commons. Where it all begins.
districts.change: Restored irrigation and open field routes

districts.name: Canopy Commons
districts.text: Dense living architecture grown around an old transport interchange. Rooftop chases and vertical fights.

districts.name: Reedwater
districts.text: Wetlands, canals, floating platforms and floodworks. Routes that follow the water.

districts.name: Glass Ridge
districts.text: Exposed slopes, energy collectors and military service roads. Ride the wind, stop the convoys.

districts.name: The Cut
districts.text: Excavated farmland and the growing data center campus. The heaviest machines live here.
districts.change: Decided by the people who live there

hidden.name: Something beneath
hidden.text: An old boundary marker on Elias's farm points down. Nobody who has followed it has said where.

cast.title: Who you fight beside, and against

people.name: Rook
people.text: Field systems specialist. Home after a failed assignment. Carries everything alone, and will have to learn not to.

people.name: Nadi Sol
people.text: Knows every shortcut and every patrol's timing. Will race you across the rooftops and win.

people.name: Elias Vale
people.text: Dry humor, meticulous records, lonely. He once allowed a survey of his land, and he has regretted it every day since.

people.name: Imani Reed
people.text: Built the first Bio-Weave interface for healing land. Watched it become armor.

people.name: Tomas Keene
people.text: Former Bastion maintenance specialist. Knows exactly where their machines are weak.

people.name: Director Mara Voss
people.text: Your old supervisor. Believes the watershed cannot survive the next crisis without her. Capable of care, and of cruelty.

commons.name: Watershed Network
commons.text: The resistance. Wants the seizures to end and the villages reconnected.

commons.name: Commons Assembly
commons.text: Keeps the settlements fed, fixed and accountable.

commons.name: Corridor Workers Union
commons.text: Wants safety and a living. A strike can stop the line, but it cannot stop the guns.

corridor.name: Bastion Directorate
corridor.text: Wants permanent control of the region. Builds the Continuity Corridor.

corridor.name: Helix Provisioning
corridor.text: Sells proprietary biology and wants communities to need it forever.

arsenal.title: Living technology. It grows as the land heals.
arsenal.intro: Everything runs on Vital Flux, drawn from living soil. Heal a place and you have more to spend. Only machines come apart in ROOTSIGNAL. People and the land are protected.

items.name: Tendril Line
items.text: Vines fire from Rook's arms. Wrap a drone and yank it in, or catch a pillar and swing with a bungee snap.

items.name: Living Staff
items.text: Fast, flowing combos on the ground and in the air. Hit at speed and it hits harder.

items.name: Mantis Strike
items.text: Pull a machine close and punch it apart. Dive out of a swing and the strike lands with everything you carried.

items.name: Kinetic Hammer
items.text: Spend Flux to launch a robot through the air, into its friends.

items.name: Layer Shield
items.text: Tap to parry, hold to raise a living wall. Tear the plating off a machine and throw it back.

items.name: Pulse Bloom
items.text: A wave of living energy that scrambles drones and cracks open armor.

items.name: Solar Glider
items.text: Leaf wings that unfold in the air. Up to twenty seconds of flight on sunlight.

atlas.title: Every species is real
atlas.intro: Look at something living and Rook scans it into the Atlas. Every plant, fungus and animal in the game is a real species, with real ecology, and a reason it lives in Greenhaven. Tap a card to turn it over.

species.name: White clover
species.fact: Bacteria in its roots fix nitrogen from the air, so it feeds the soil around it.
species.greenhaven: Sown between the terrace rows as living fertiliser. Greenhaven buys no nitrogen.

species.name: Scarlet runner bean
species.fact: Another nitrogen fixer. Its flowers feed bees and, at home, hummingbirds.
species.greenhaven: The dried beans are a winter staple at the long tables.

species.name: Apricot
species.fact: Its early blossom is one of the first big meals of the year for bees.
species.greenhaven: Anyone may pick from the public trees on the avenue.

species.name: English lavender
species.fact: Drought tolerant and loved by bees and butterflies.
species.greenhaven: The purple drifts on the roofs are there for the pollinators first.

species.name: Valley oak
species.fact: One old oak can support hundreds of species of insects, birds and fungi.
species.greenhaven: The village was built around the heritage oak, not over it.

species.name: Chicken of the woods
species.fact: A wood rotting fungus that turns dead heartwood back into soil.
species.greenhaven: Left alone on the old logs. Only trained foragers pick it.

species.name: Oyster mushroom
species.fact: One of the few fungi that traps tiny nematodes for nitrogen.
species.greenhaven: Grown on spent straw from the terraces, then the straw goes back to the soil.

species.name: Western honey bee
species.fact: A colony of tens of thousands pollinates crops and wild flowers for kilometres.
species.greenhaven: The hives sit on the green roofs.

species.name: Monarch butterfly
species.fact: Its caterpillars eat only milkweed. Some migrate thousands of kilometres.
species.greenhaven: Milkweed grows wild along the river so the monarchs keep coming through.

species.name: Great blue heron
species.fact: Stands still in shallow water and strikes fast. A sign of a living river.
species.greenhaven: It came back the year the river was restored.

species.name: Green tree frog
species.fact: Breathes partly through its skin, so it needs clean water.
species.greenhaven: They sit on the solar lily pads, which make warm perches.

species.name: Common eastern firefly
species.fact: The flashes are courtship. Light pollution and pesticides make them vanish.
species.greenhaven: The terraces stay dark and unsprayed after sunset for them.

community.title: Follow, play, back it
community.intro: ROOTSIGNAL is made by a tiny team in the open. Every follow, playtest and share decides how fast it grows.

playtest.title: Play it before anyone else
playtest.intro: The first playtest is small. Sign up and you get the build by email, a controls card, and a short form to tell me what felt good and what broke.
playtest.note: Mac first. Windows is next, and browser play after that. Sign up on any computer and you will hear when your version is ready.
playtest.sent_text: I will email you when the next build is ready for your computer. Check your spam folder just in case.

feedback.title: Already played?
feedback.intro: Tell me what happened. Short is fine. Every answer is read.
